q1: SELECT NAME FROM SALESPERSON AS S WHERE 0 = ( SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ORDERS AS O JOIN COMPANY AS C ON O.COM_ID = C.COM_ID WHERE O.SALES_ID = S.SALES_ID AND C.NAME = 'RED' )
q2: SELECT S.NAME FROM SALESPERSON S WHERE S.SALES_ID NOT IN (SELECT SALES_ID FROM ORDERS O1 JOIN COMPANY C1 ON O1.COM_ID = C1.COM_ID WHERE C1.NAME='RED' )

q2_prompt_sql: SELECT S.NAME FROM SALESPERSON S WHERE S.SALES_ID NOT IN (SELECT SALES_ID FROM ORDERS O1 JOIN COMPANY C1 ON O1.COM_ID = C1.COM_ID WHERE C1.NAME='RED' )
explanation: Q1 checks for salespersons who have zero orders associated with the company named 'RED'. Q2 excludes salespersons who have any order associated with the company named 'RED'. The difference arises when a salesperson has no orders at all (including no orders with 'RED'). In such a case, Q1 will include them (since count is zero), but Q2 will not exclude them since SALES_ID will not appear in the subquery result. This leads to different results.
counterexample_dsp: A salesperson with no orders at all will be included by Q1 but not by Q2.
